null.message: Notification "rule-null" trigger.type must be one of [created, updated, transition, scheduled, threshold, calculatedChange], or the trigger must name an app-defined event as a namespaced string (e.g. "booking.confirmed").

event-empty-string.message: Notification "rule-event-empty-string" declares an app event that is not a non-empty string.

event-reserved.message: Notification "rule-event-reserved" names "created" as an app event, but that is a reserved trigger type; use the object form {"type": "created"} instead.

event-no-dot.message: Notification "rule-event-no-dot" app event "Booking" must be namespaced with a dot and start lowercase (e.g. "booking.confirmed", "lifecycle.optIn"), so it can never collide with a reserved trigger type.

event-upper-start.message: Notification "rule-event-upper-start" app event "Booking.confirmed" must be namespaced with a dot and start lowercase (e.g. "booking.confirmed", "lifecycle.optIn"), so it can never collide with a reserved trigger type.

event-trailing-dot.message: Notification "rule-event-trailing-dot" app event "booking." must be namespaced with a dot and start lowercase (e.g. "booking.confirmed", "lifecycle.optIn"), so it can never collide with a reserved trigger type.

event-underscore.message: Notification "rule-event-underscore" app event "booking.con_firmed" must be namespaced with a dot and start lowercase (e.g. "booking.confirmed", "lifecycle.optIn"), so it can never collide with a reserved trigger type.

Notification "rule-event-object-reserved" trigger.type=threshold trigger.op must be one of [gt, gte, lt, lte, eq, ne]; got "".

sched-filter-string.message: Notification "rule-sched-filter-string" trigger.filter must be an object/map.

sched-filter-bad.message: Notification "rule-sched-filter-bad" trigger.filter.status is a map without an "operator" key; it is neither a scalar, a list, nor an operator object.

sched-dedupe-string.message: Notification "rule-sched-dedupe-string" trigger.dedupeFields must be a non-empty array of strings.
